name: A re-review asked for on an unchanged commit silently does nothing
description:
A partner can ask for a re-review by commenting on the pull request. If they ask on a commit we have already reviewed, the tool today does nothing at all — no answer, no result, no explanation. From the partner's side it simply looks broken.

It should not run a fresh review either, and for two separate reasons. The code is byte-for-byte what we already read, so a second pass cannot reach a different answer and would only cost money. And under the rule that a finding is closed only by a real change in the code, a commit with no changes cannot close anything anyway.

So the answer becomes deterministic: we tell the partner there are no new commits since the one we reviewed.

**Update after build:** a claim that something was fixed still always gets a proper reply — but only when it is written as its own comment, separate from the `/rereview` one. Text added after the `/rereview` line, on that same comment, is not read by anything today: a comment is classified as either a command or a claim, never both, so nothing looks at what follows the command. Answering that combined case is left for later — noted with a TODO in the code at the point it would matter, not built here.

One thing stays exactly as it is today: if part of the earlier round crashed, asking again still retries the part that died. "No new review" means no second pass over what already succeeded, not abandoning what failed.

**Done when:** a re-review asked for on an unchanged commit answers the partner instead of doing nothing, never starts a fresh review over code it has already read, and still recovers a round that failed halfway.

Plan: https://github.com/shoptet/aidev-apps/pull/27 — batch 2, task T11. Independent of everything else in batch 2.
